groups.title: Participant reflections
groups.description: What participants took away, from testing and human understanding to organizational change.

mentions.author: Toni Hintikka
mentions.summary: Detailed Finnish reflection on organizational settings, documentation, acceptance criteria and enforced agent boundaries; advocates measuring idea-to-production time, rework, quality and customer impact; recommends the recording.
mentions.context: Participant reflection, summarized from Finnish.

mentions.author: Kaisa Tirkkonen
mentions.summary: Highlights autonomy between human approval gates, clear problem descriptions, validation and automated testing; thanks speakers and organizers.
mentions.context: Participant reflection on quality and accountability.

mentions.author: Mikko Paloheimo
mentions.summary: Appreciated testing and quality throughout the talks; took several pages of notes back to his team and organization; valued discussions and networking.
mentions.context: Reports plans to apply the learning; implementation and resulting benefits have not been established.

mentions.author: Jenna Kaisanlahti
mentions.summary: Compares AI adoption with remote work: individual efficiency can harm organizational outcomes when implemented poorly; appreciates academic perspectives.
mentions.context: Participant reflection on organizational effects and the research–practice mix.

mentions.author: Visa Linkiö
mentions.affiliation: CTO and AI transformation advisor; participant
mentions.summary: Praises the programme from business intent through production and maintenance; discusses moving bottlenecks, broader contributions, code understanding, discovery and leadership.
mentions.context: Participant reflection. A further comment on curation appears below.

mentions.author: Heimo Laukkanen
mentions.summary: Praises the talks and Sini's message that software development fundamentals matter more with AI.
mentions.context: Event-day reaction. Mikko Vaha adds a qualification about engineering fundamentals below.

mentions.author: Jaakko Hollmén
mentions.summary: Adds reflections about decentralized AI, people as creators, care for people and human understanding of code.
mentions.context: This summary covers the addition made after the seminar; the opening of the post was written before it.

mentions.author: Oskari Liukkonen
mentions.summary: Highlights Mo's automotive analogy and the need to rethink processes through Lean principles.
mentions.context: Event-related reflection. The discussion also includes comments from Anna Kholina and Ville Takanen.

mentions.author: Moses Nderemani
mentions.summary: Praises organization, presentations and conversations; describes his recommender-systems poster and shares its materials.
mentions.context: Participation as a poster presenter is explicit.

mentions.author: Mikko Vaha
mentions.summary: Reports insights and ideas to develop at SOK.
mentions.context: His reported 20+ pages of notes cover both SDLCAI and SOK’s AI conference. His slide criticism is included below.

mentions.author: Sachin Kundu
mentions.summary: Praises organization, conversations and Mo's presentation, but reports no new ideas for an experienced practitioner; criticizes text-heavy slides and AI-factory hype; discusses costs, verification, review queues and changing roles.
mentions.context: A mixed assessment from an attendee. His praise of one talk coexists with criticism of the programme; his impressions of other attendees are a personal account.

mentions.author: Pasi Vuorio — thematic synthesis
mentions.summary: Created a thematic synthesis of the ten presentations with Claude, mapping agreement and possible points of debate; praises the presentations and discussions and reports useful ideas for the ModernPath team.
mentions.context: A participant-created interpretation made with Claude, rather than a speaker-approved transcript. Measured business outcomes have not been established.

mentions.author: Hilkka Huotari
mentions.affiliation: Participant with Wonna; technology-sponsor connection disclosed
mentions.summary: Would choose SDLCAI over WeAreDevelopers after attending both; values the research–practice mix, varied talks matching their descriptions, absence of unexpected sponsor pitches, manageable scale, food, networking and a ticket under €100; hopes the seminar returns.
mentions.context: Participant assessment with a sponsor connection. The conference comparison reflects her personal experience. Summarized from Finnish.

groups.title: Speaker and research reflections
groups.description: Speakers and their institutions reflect on their contributions and the discussions around them.

mentions.author: Mo Khazali
mentions.summary: Uses Lean and automotive lessons to discuss bottlenecks; advocates observing real work and measuring flow, outcomes and customer value; thanks organizers and audience.
mentions.context: A speaker’s own reflection. The discussion by Theodo colleagues is listed separately below.

mentions.author: Jenni Kylmäkoski
mentions.summary: Appreciates talks without unnecessary hype; highlights Kaizen, Five Whys, AI communities, plan reviews and developer oversight of broader contributions.
mentions.context: A speaker’s own reflection.

mentions.author: Viljami Kuosmanen
mentions.summary: Describes challenging Q&A about non-engineers contributing to a production codebase; praises the seminar, panel and several other talks.
mentions.context: A speaker’s account of audience debate; it does not by itself validate the approach presented.

mentions.author: Jussi Hacklin
mentions.summary: Praises talks, discussions and organization after presenting regulated-domain adoption; hopes the event becomes annual.
mentions.context: A speaker’s own reflection.

mentions.author: Sini Tistelgrén
mentions.summary: Praises sharp audience questions and conversations.
mentions.context: A speaker’s own reflection, alongside a related post by her company Aimbition.

mentions.author: Tapio Pitkäranta
mentions.summary: Connects his presentation to the Agentic Probe paper and thanks participants for discussions of agentic discovery and engineering.
mentions.context: A speaker’s research-to-practice follow-up.

mentions.author: Muhammad Waseem
mentions.summary: Describes valuable industry–academia conversations and ideas to bring back to GPT-Lab.
mentions.context: A speaker’s personal account, covering the same contribution as GPT-Lab’s institutional recap.

mentions.author: GPT-Lab
mentions.summary: Summarizes Waseem's keynote on understanding, review, system safety, architecture and learning as code generation becomes cheaper.
mentions.context: An institutional account of its own speaker’s contribution.

mentions.author: Ohans Emmanuel
mentions.summary: Praises the organization and fellow speakers; reflects on shipping changes to large brownfield production systems at agent speed while preserving quality, and reports that other teams converged on similar foundational principles.
mentions.context: Speaker reflection. The post does not establish measured evidence of unchanged incident rates.

mentions.author: Mo Khazali — keynote video follow-up
mentions.affiliation: Theodo; keynote speaker; author of the reflection above
mentions.summary: Publishes the first excerpt from “1978: The Last Good Year”, contrasting automation investment with improvements to the production system and relating the analogy to AI adoption in software; announces further excerpts.
mentions.context: Content follow-through from the speaker already represented here. Further excerpts were announced but have not been verified.

groups.title: Sponsor and company follow-through
groups.description: Company accounts, event-day notes and reported activity after the seminar. Sponsor relationships are stated with each author.

mentions.author: Wunderdog
mentions.summary: Says the event delivered grounded, practical and honest discussion; highlights controlled non-engineer contributions, plan reviews and measured productivity; hopes for another edition.
mentions.context: The company was the event’s main sponsor.

mentions.author: Wonna — exploring the future of coding
mentions.summary: Reports two skills under development the following day: quiz-me helps developers maintain application understanding; review-index identifies material for human review. Praises curation, conversations and free content.
mentions.context: The company reports that most of its staff attended. These are reported experiments; measured long-term benefits have not been established.

mentions.author: Aimbition
mentions.summary: Emphasizes independent checks, accountability, lead time, change failure rate and cost per accepted change.
mentions.context: A company post related to cofounder and speaker Sini Tistelgrén’s reflection.

mentions.author: Ville Komulainen — morning notes
mentions.summary: Discusses measured versus perceived productivity and plan reviews.
mentions.context: Event-day notes from the main sponsor’s CEO; the afternoon notes are a separate entry by the same author.

mentions.author: Ville Komulainen — afternoon notes
mentions.summary: Discusses production validation and engineering controls enabling non-engineers to contribute.
mentions.context: A continuation of the morning notes by the same author.

mentions.author: Mikko Vallaskivi
mentions.summary: Says Mo's and Ohans's talks resonated with daily work, solutions and hurdles; mentions meeting people and the sponsor table.
mentions.context: Event-day presence is explicit; the author works for the main sponsor.

mentions.author: Ville Komulainen — post-event tech talk
mentions.summary: Reports a facilitated Friday discussion of SDLCAI findings: abstraction in pull requests and technical-design / architecture quality. Recommends continuous adjustment as tools change.
mentions.context: Reports a company discussion after the seminar. Measured delivery improvements have not been established.

groups.title: Constructive criticism and nuance
groups.description: Questions about the examples, terminology and engineering assumptions discussed during the day. Sachin Kundu’s mixed overall review is also included in participant reflections.

mentions.author: Anssi Lehtelä
mentions.summary: Questions a slide's portrayal of roles, sequential work, late testing and output tracking rather than shared outcomes.
mentions.context: Attendance is unverified. The photographed slide presented a simplified current-practice baseline, rather than recommending late testing.

mentions.author: Mikko Vaha
mentions.summary: Agrees with Anssi's concerns and says the slide's problems were why he photographed it.
mentions.context: This specific criticism coexists with his positive overall reflection. The slide presented a simplified current-practice baseline, rather than recommending late testing.

mentions.author: Mikko Vaha
mentions.summary: Observes that engineering fundamentals have always been challenging.
mentions.context: A participant’s qualification about longstanding engineering challenges.

mentions.author: Sami Kuhmonen
mentions.summary: Jokes about a refund / false advertising because deployment checks mean the example was not really vibe coding; Viljami replies about code the author cannot read.
mentions.context: Attendance is unverified. The exchange reads as humour; no actual refund complaint was established.

mentions.author: Christoph Klink
mentions.summary: Describes accelerating change as difficult to predict even six weeks ahead and appreciates Ohans’s role in shaping perspectives.
mentions.context: Discussion under Ohans’s reflection. Attendance and recording viewing are unverified.

mentions.author: Lauri Suomalainen, with Niko Kivelä’s reply
mentions.affiliation: Teamit; Lauri’s SOK AI Conf presentation is cited in Niko’s post
mentions.summary: Asks whether enabling agents is mainly an implementation challenge or a strategy challenge; Niko agrees that the distinction belongs in the thought process.
mentions.context: One discussion record under Niko Kivelä’s post. Lauri’s presentation was at SOK AI Conf; SDLCAI attendance is unverified. The link opens the containing comment thread.

mentions.author: Niko Nousiainen, with Niko Kivelä’s reply
mentions.affiliation: Hidden Trail; no event affiliation established
mentions.summary: Distinguishes humans using AI interfaces from agents using system interfaces and expresses concern about direct AI-to-AI interaction. Niko Kivelä questions the boundary between another agent and a system interface, using an MCP endpoint as an example.
mentions.context: One conceptual discussion record including the author’s response. Attendance and recording viewing are unverified. The link opens the containing comment thread.
